TOMORROW at Patch Bay: From Lore to Logic: Building Interactive Worlds with AI + Figma, led by Erik B.

In this hands-on workshop, Erik B. will lead from story and concept to working prototype using Figma, AI, and vibe coding. Using his civic simulation project Supertino as a case study, we’ll build out the storyboard, UX, narrative, characters, and visual assets, team up with a large language model to turn behaviors and interactions into code and logic, and bring it all together into an interactive prototype.

We’ll wrap with Q&A, troubleshooting, and an honest conversation about where these tools shine, where they break, and how to use them more intentionally.

Come through tomorrow night and build something with us!

caption:
What's your perfect weekend in the Presidio?

Here are a few of our favorites, but don't take our word for it, there's something for every art, nature, history, and food lover! 

Friday
📚 Start your national park adventures at the Presidio Visitor Center — with interactive displays, maps and books, it's perfect way to spend a slow Friday afternoon.
🎨 Head to The Walt Disney Family Museum for the opening of Awakening Beauty: The Art of Eyvind Earle — the visionary artist behind the iconic look of Sleeping Beauty. 
🌅 End the evening at The Mess Hall for dinner and a sunset over the Golden Gate that will genuinely stop you mid-bite. Order something from the full bar. Stay until the light goes golden. You earned it.

Saturday
☕ Start the morning at Dalida for brunch — one of the most beautiful restaurants in San Francisco, right inside a national park side. Order something with the wild pistachio oat milk coffee. You will not regret it.
🎨 Head over to Sports Basement for ArtSpan SF Open Studios — a rare chance to meet Bay Area artists up close, see work in progress, and bring something home. Free and open all weekend.
🌲 Spend the afternoon exploring on foot. The Coastal Trail to Baker Beach. Crissy Marsh if the birds are moving through. Take your time, it's the weekend. 

Sunday
🧘 Start with Free Community Yoga at Outpost Meadow — one hour, all levels, surrounded by the Presidio's open sky. Bring your mat and arrive a few minutes early.
🏛️ Join a Ranger-Led Walk at Presidio Tunnel Tops celebrating the Presidio's 250th Anniversary — a guided half-mile loop through the Main Post tracing 250 years of history from the Ohlone people through the Spanish, Mexican, and U.S. Army eras to today. Free. Fascinating. Not to be missed.
🌮 End the weekend with margaritas and guacamole at Colibri or grab something from Presidio Pop Up and find a picnic table with a view that makes you never want to leave.

Can you believe all of this is available in a national park site, just minutes from San Francisco? Start exploring the Presidio at www.presidio.gov

Conservative activist Christopher F. Rufo posted a video on Sept. 30 with the faces of more than a dozen residents of 111 Taylor and wrote, “EXCLUSIVE: California is dumping convicted pedophiles into residential neighborhoods in San Francisco.” ⁠

Lots of reactionary stuff here. Research suggests that limitations on where sex offenders can live actually makes them more likely to reoffend.

Quick history on why this is legal:

In 2006, California voters passed Prop 83 (Jessica's Law) with 70% of the vote. It banned registered sex offenders from living within 2,000 feet of any school or park. State maps showed that in San Francisco, almost nowhere residential was left.

The day after the election, a federal judge in SF blocked it as likely unconstitutional. In 2007 another federal judge ruled it couldn't apply to anyone convicted before it passed. Then in 2015, the CA Supreme Court ruled unanimously in In re Taylor that blanket enforcement on parolees was unconstitutional. The evidence showed it pushed hundreds of offenders into homelessness, which made them harder to track and the public less safe, not more.

Today, parole can still restrict where someone lives, but only case by case. And the original law never covered daycares at all, only schools and parks.

So the gap isn't an accident. Voters tried, the courts struck it down, and nothing replaced it. If you want it changed, the people to call are your state legislators, not City Hall.

caption:
Today, October 23rd we celebrate Bobby Hutcherson Day in San Francisco!

The most accomplished vibraphonist and composer to emerge in the latter half of the 20th Century, #BobbyHutcherson redefined the role of the instrument in modern jazz, bringing new levels of technical mastery and harmonic sophistication. He enjoyed an unprecedented 24-year association with the Blue Note Records label, making indelible contributions to over 250 albums during his Blue Note tenure and leading 23 recordings that introduced the world to the standards “Little B’s Poem,” “Bouquet,” “Components,” “Montara,” and others.

In 2010, the National Endowment for the Arts named Bobby an NEA Jazz Master for his lifetime of contributions to the art form – the highest honor the U.S. bestows on jazz musicians. A great friend and artist with a long history performing on SFJAZZ stages, beginning with a performance at the very first Jazz in the City Festival in 1983, Bobby was a founding member of the SFJAZZ Collective – composing, arranging, and performing with the band from its inception in 2004 through 2007.

caption:
Every Saturday - and every first and third Wednesday - something quiet and remarkable happens at the Presidio. 

Strangers show up. From across the Bay, from different neighborhoods, different backgrounds, different reasons for being here. Most of them don't know each other. But they have one thing in common: they love this place and they want to take care of it.

Together they pull invasive plants, restore native habitats, and help bring back the forests, wildflowers, and wetlands that make the Presidio one of the most biologically diverse national park sites in the country. 

You won't read about them in the headlines. But walk these trails through the wildflowers, past the wetlands, under the canopy of a forest slowly becoming what it was always meant to be, and you are walking through their work.

Nearly three decades of this. Park ecologists and volunteers, side by side, quietly doing the work the rest of us get to enjoy.

Want to be part of it? No experience needed. Just show up, get your hands dirty, and spend a few hours outside in one of the most extraordinary places in California doing something that genuinely matters.

SFJAZZ is proud to present Roopa in Flux, an innovative ensemble fusing South Indian Carnatic classical vocal traditions with soul, free improvisation, and jazz-inflected interplay in the intimate setting of the Joe Henderson Lab to kick off the month of November. 

Led by Bay Area-reared vocalist Roopa Mahadevan, a featured soloist on Christopher Tin’s GRAMMY-winning Calling All Dawns, this dynamic ensemble represents one of the most adventurous voices in contemporary global music. Rooted in the rigorous, microtonal vocal ornaments (gamakas) and complex rhythmic structures (tala) of South Indian Carnatic classical tradition, Mahadevan fearlessly bridges ancestral heritage with modern cross-genre exploration alongside virtuosic mridangam master Rohan Krishnamurthy. 

Don't miss an evening of emotionally charged improvisation, intricate polyrhythms, and cross-cultural storytelling exploring themes of identity, migration, and joy.

caption:
Did you know that 2026 is the 25th anniversary of 7x7?
.
We spent the afternoon digging through the archives, beginning with our very first issue in 2001. 
.
For the first decade, 7x7 was a big, glossy magazine with celebrity interviews, professional photo shoots, and the other hallmarks of the early 2000s. 
.
After running for several years in the 2010s as both a magazine and a website, the changing media landscape led us to say goodbye to the hard copy version in 2015.
.
But while many of the Bay Area publications we came up with never made it over the hump, here we are still kicking 🦵⚽️
.
Join us this Saturday, October 24th, @ritualcoffee on Valencia Street as we reveal some of the gems we uncovered from our last 25 years at the @litquake LitCrawl. We'll be reading from the archives starting at 6:30pm.

caption:
Opening January 16, 2027 at Yerba Buena Center for the Arts: “Barbara Stauffacher Solomon: Why? Why Not?”

Barbara Stauffacher Solomon became famous almost overnight in 1966, when she painted giant letters, stripes, and arrows across the walls at The Sea Ranch. Yet her whole practice—as an artist, designer, writer, architect, and landscape theorist—has never been seen in full. 

“Barbara Stauffacher Solomon: Why? Why Not?” brings a wide body of work together for the first time since her death. Trained in Swiss graphic design in Basel and later in architecture at Berkeley, Stauffacher Solomon produced prolifically for over 60 years: everything from books to Supergraphics, from landscape drawings to paintings of ping-pong tables, all relevant to the time in which she lived. 

Drawing on rarely seen material from her estate’s archive and a new Supergraphic realized from her designs on YBCA’s walls, the exhibition takes visitors on a journey from Swiss grids to California freeways. Read more about the exhibition at YBCA.org or via link in bio. 

-
"Barbara Stauffacher Solomon: Why? Why Not?" is guest curated by Martin Strickland. 

Artwork images courtesy of the Estate of Barbara Stauffacher Solomon, Anthony Meier, Mill Valley, and von Bartha, Basel.
